questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the National Housing Authority (NHA)?

options.text: Regulates and licenses subdivision developers, ensuring compliance with national standards
Builds and develops government housing projects for low-income families
Finances housing loans for individual end-buyers, providing financial support for home ownership
Coordinates inter-agency housing policy to streamline efforts across different government bodies

rationale.a: That is DHSUD's role (formerly HLURB)—regulation and licensing of developers under PD 957.
rationale.b: NHA is the government housing PRODUCER—it builds resettlement projects, medium-rise housing, core housing, and slum upgrading programs. Production (building units) is its defining function.
rationale.c: That is Pag-IBIG/HDMF, SSS, and GSIS—they finance loans. NHA does not issue loans; it constructs units.
rationale.d: That was historically HUDCC's role (now absorbed into DHSUD).
rationale.correct: NHA is the government housing PRODUCER—it builds resettlement projects, medium-rise housing, core housing, and slum upgrading programs. Production (building units) is its defining function.
rationale.takeaway: NHA = producer (builds). Finance agencies = Pag-IBIG, SSS, GSIS.

questions.text: If NHA constructs 500 units of medium-rise socialized housing and allocates them to informal settlers from a danger area, and separately, SHFC finances a community mortgage allowing 200 households to purchase their occupied land, which statement most accurately characterizes these two interventions?

options.text: Both are identical government programs serving the same population through the same mechanism, which is incorrect.
NHA intervention is relocation with new housing supply; SHFC intervention enables in-situ tenure formalization—different mechanisms addressing different community preferences
SHFC's program is superior because it requires no government funding, which is a misunderstanding of the program's funding structure.
NHA's intervention is problematic because it does not allow communities to remain in place, which oversimplifies the issue.

rationale.a: They are entirely different—different agencies, different mechanisms, different outcomes.
rationale.b: The two interventions serve fundamentally different purposes: NHA provides new housing in resettlement (for communities that must move due to danger); SHFC enables communities to formalize tenure and stay in place. Choice between them depends on context and community preference.
rationale.c: SHFC programs require government financing through loan portfolios; they are not zero-cost.
rationale.d: NHA programs are appropriate for danger area relocations where in-situ options are unsafe.
rationale.correct: The two interventions serve fundamentally different purposes: NHA provides new housing in resettlement (for communities that must move due to danger); SHFC enables communities to formalize tenure and stay in place. Choice between them depends on context and community preference.
rationale.takeaway: NHA = resettlement production; SHFC = in-situ tenure formalization. Complementary, not redundant.

questions.text: What distinguishes the Community Mortgage Program (CMP) from other government housing programs?

options.text: It is administered by Pag-IBIG and available to individual salaried workers, providing a unique financing option for home ownership
It allows communities to collectively mortgage land they occupy, enabling in-situ upgrading without relocation
It is a direct grant program requiring no repayment from beneficiaries, offering financial relief to low-income families
It is funded by the national government and administered by NHA, focusing on large-scale housing projects

rationale.a: Pag-IBIG administers individual housing loans, not CMP. CMP is SHFC's community program.
rationale.b: The CMP, administered by SHFC, is designed for communities—not individuals. It finances collective land purchases through a single mortgage secured by the community organization, preserving existing settlements.
rationale.c: CMP is a mortgage program (repayment required), not a grant.
rationale.d: CMP is SHFC's program. NHA builds housing directly; it does not administer the CMP.
rationale.correct: The CMP, administered by SHFC, is designed for communities—not individuals. It finances collective land purchases through a single mortgage secured by the community organization, preserving existing settlements.
rationale.takeaway: CMP is community-based collective financing (SHFC); preserves communities in-situ.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes between NHA and SHFC in terms of their roles in government housing?

options.text: NHA finances housing loans; SHFC builds housing units, focusing on urban areas with high-density requirements
NHA regulates developers; SHFC oversees zoning compliance, ensuring adherence to local government unit ordinances
NHA builds and develops housing; SHFC finances community-based housing programs
Both are regulatory agencies with overlapping authority, often collaborating on joint housing initiatives

rationale.a: This reverses their roles. NHA produces; SHFC finances.
rationale.b: DHSUD regulates developers. Neither NHA nor SHFC is regulatory.
rationale.c: NHA's role is production (building); SHFC's role is financing (enabling communities to buy land or access housing through CMP).
rationale.d: Neither is regulatory. NHA is a developer/builder; SHFC is a finance institution.
rationale.correct: NHA's role is production (building); SHFC's role is financing (enabling communities to buy land or access housing through CMP).
rationale.takeaway: Producer (NHA) vs. Financer (SHFC)—complementary roles, never confused.

questions.text: An informal settler community in a flood-prone area wants to purchase the land they occupy to prevent relocation. Which agency's program would be most appropriate to facilitate this?

options.text: NHA—through direct government funding and unit construction
SHFC—through the Community Mortgage Program
Pag-IBIG—through individual socialized housing loans
DHSUD—through relocation site designation

rationale.a: NHA builds housing but does not finance land purchases for existing communities.
rationale.b: SHFC's CMP finances community land purchases through collective mortgages, allowing the community to buy the land and avoid relocation while upgrading in place.
rationale.c: Pag-IBIG is for individual workers' housing loans, not community land purchases.
rationale.d: DHSUD regulates housing and CLUPs; it does not provide financing or relocation programs.
rationale.correct: SHFC's CMP finances community land purchases through collective mortgages, allowing the community to buy the land and avoid relocation while upgrading in place.
rationale.takeaway: For communities to buy their own land (in-situ): SHFC/CMP is the enabling mechanism.

questions.text: Comparing the scope of beneficiaries: NHA primarily serves low-income populations through production, while Pag-IBIG primarily serves employed individuals through financing. Why is this distinction important for Philippine housing policy?

options.text: It ensures that both low-income informal settlers and formal employees have access to housing through different mechanisms
It eliminates the need for private housing developers, which is a misconception as private developers play a crucial role
It removes the responsibility of government to serve market-rate buyers, focusing resources on those who need assistance
It concentrates all housing responsibility in a single agency, which is not the case as multiple agencies are involved

rationale.a: The division of roles ensures comprehensive coverage: NHA serves those unable to access market financing (informal settlers, very low-income families); Pag-IBIG serves the employed sector. Together, they address different segments of housing need.
rationale.b: Private developers remain important for open-market housing—PD 957 regulates them.
rationale.c: Market-rate buyers are served by private developers and Pag-IBIG's open-market loan tier.
rationale.d: The system is deliberately distributed across multiple agencies for different functions.
rationale.correct: The division of roles ensures comprehensive coverage: NHA serves those unable to access market financing (informal settlers, very low-income families); Pag-IBIG serves the employed sector. Together, they address different segments of housing need.
rationale.takeaway: NHA + Pag-IBIG + SHFC = layered system serving different population segments.

questions.text: Why is the Community Mortgage Program (CMP) considered one of the most successful housing interventions for informal settlers compared to forced relocation?

options.text: It transfers all government responsibility to the private sector, reducing public expenditure on housing
It preserves existing community networks and social capital while enabling formal land tenure through collective mortgages
It eliminates the need for government investment in housing, allowing funds to be redirected to other public services
It converts informal settlers into formal employees with government contracts, providing stable income sources

rationale.a: CMP is government-financed through SHFC, though the community bears the mortgage obligation.
rationale.b: CMP's success lies in enabling communities to formalize tenure while remaining in place—preserving livelihoods, kinship networks, and social stability. This aligns with research by John Turner and others on the value of community-based housing solutions.
rationale.c: CMP requires government investment through SHFC financing.
rationale.d: CMP does not change employment status; it enables land formalization.
rationale.correct: CMP's success lies in enabling communities to formalize tenure while remaining in place—preserving livelihoods, kinship networks, and social stability. This aligns with research by John Turner and others on the value of community-based housing solutions.
rationale.takeaway: CMP success = in-situ tenure security + community preservation + social stability.

questions.text: A low-income family receives an NHA resettlement unit with title in their name. Under which type of NHA program would they most likely qualify for such direct housing production?

options.text: Open-market housing financing, which typically requires higher income levels and credit scores
Community Mortgage Program, designed for collective land acquisition but not direct housing production
Government resettlement projects for informal settlers
Commercial condominium development, which is not typically associated with low-income housing initiatives

rationale.a: Open-market financing is Pag-IBIG's role, not NHA's.
rationale.b: CMP is SHFC's program for land purchase, not NHA's.
rationale.c: NHA's primary mission is direct housing production for low-income families, particularly resettlement of informal settlers from danger areas or development sites. Receiving a completed unit with title is characteristic of NHA resettlement programs.
rationale.d: NHA does not develop commercial projects.
rationale.correct: NHA's primary mission is direct housing production for low-income families, particularly resettlement of informal settlers from danger areas or development sites. Receiving a completed unit with title is characteristic of NHA resettlement programs.
rationale.takeaway: NHA resettlement = direct government production, not loan-based.

questions.text: A young engineer working for a private corporation needs a housing loan to buy a condominium unit in Metro Manila. Which agency provides this type of individual end-buyer financing?

options.text: NHA—through medium-rise housing programs under the National Resettlement Program
SHFC—through the Community Mortgage Program for organized informal settler groups
Pag-IBIG (HDMF)—through open-market or low-cost housing loans
DHSUD—through approved developer projects under Balanced Housing compliance

rationale.a: NHA produces government-built housing, not finance for market purchases.
rationale.b: SHFC/CMP is for communities, not individuals.
rationale.c: Pag-IBIG/HDMF provides housing loans to individual employees (private and government sectors). Open-market housing loans cover purchases up to ₱6 million, appropriate for a condo purchase.
rationale.d: DHSUD regulates; it does not finance purchases.
rationale.correct: Pag-IBIG/HDMF provides housing loans to individual employees (private and government sectors). Open-market housing loans cover purchases up to ₱6 million, appropriate for a condo purchase.
rationale.takeaway: Individual employee housing loans: Pag-IBIG (employed), SSS (private sector), GSIS (government).

questions.text: A barangay is planning an in-situ upgrading project for an informal settler community on municipally-owned land. Which combination of agencies would be essential partners in this effort?

options.text: NHA (to build) and DHSUD (to approve zoning), ensuring compliance with local development plans
SHFC/CMP (to finance land or housing improvement) and the local government (to provide the land)
Pag-IBIG (to provide loans) and NHA (to build all units), focusing on affordable housing solutions
DHSUD (to regulate) and GSIS (to finance government employee housing), which may not directly address informal settler needs

rationale.a: While DHSUD approval may be needed, NHA is unnecessary if the community finances their own upgrade via CMP.
rationale.b: In-situ upgrading requires financing for community land acquisition or housing improvement (SHFC/CMP) and local government support to make land available. This is the classic SHFC/CMP deployment model.
rationale.c: Pag-IBIG serves individual employees, not communities. NHA is not required for community-financed upgrades.
rationale.d: GSIS is for government employees only. DHSUD's role is ancillary here (approval/regulation).
rationale.correct: In-situ upgrading requires financing for community land acquisition or housing improvement (SHFC/CMP) and local government support to make land available. This is the classic SHFC/CMP deployment model.
rationale.takeaway: In-situ upgrading = SHFC/CMP + local government land partnership.
